issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies over all f in C([0,1]^d), including f identically zero. For f = 0 item (iii) is impossible for any choice of affine maps: ||f_1||_p = 0, so ||f_2||_p < ||f_1||_p cannot hold; the construction itself gives M_f = M_{-f} = 0, hence both cutoff families are empty and n = 0, contradicting n in N^+. The same omitted hypothesis affects the iteration: if any intermediate residual f_{n_1+...+1} is identically zero (which the proof does not exclude), Theorem 3.1 cannot be reapplied and strict decrease in Theorem 1.1 (ii) fails from that point on.

issues.title: Strict monotonicity claims fail for the zero function and for vanishing intermediate residuals
issues.why_classification: A standard degenerate-case hypothesis and a nonzero-residual qualifier resolve it; the method, the contraction factor, and every substantive guarantee for nonzero targets survive with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: At k = 1 the update h_1 = A^{out}_1 o ReLU o A_1 is a one-hidden-layer ReLU network. Take d >= 2 and a nonzero continuous f >= 0 compactly supported in the open cube (0,1)^d (e.g., a bump). Pointwise domination (ii) at k = 1 forces 0 <= h_1 <= 2f on [0,1]^d, so h_1 vanishes on the open shell surrounding supp f. Every ReLU unit of h_1 has a constant gradient jump along its whole kink hyperplane; any hyperplane meeting the interior of supp f also meets the shell (hyperplanes are unbounded and the shell separates the support from the cube boundary), where h_1 = 0 forces the jump to be zero. Hence h_1 has no kinks near the support, is affine there, and vanishes on its boundary, so h_1 = 0 on [0,1]^d, giving ||f_2||_p = ||f_1||_p in contradiction with (iii) at k = 1. Thus (iii) is false as stated in d >= 2; the obstruction is the architecture, not the proof. (In d = 1 one-hidden-layer hat functions resolve it.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken (iii) to k = 2,...,n and take a trivial first update (e.g., A_1 carrying the input with A^{out}_1 = 0); Theorem 1.1 then survives verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.1 (iii) is false at k = 1 for interior-supported targets in dimension d >= 2. No other labelled result is damaged: Theorem 1.1's strictness ||R_{k+1}||_p < ||R_k||_p for k >= 1 involves only updates of depth >= 2, which can localize, so it is unaffected once (iii) is weakened.
issues.title: Strict L^p decrease at the first grade is unattainable with one-hidden-layer updates in d >= 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line quantifier change plus a trivial first grade; it provably loses no achievable content (the k = 1 instance is impossible in the stated architecture) and every downstream claim, including Theorem 1.1, is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: Stage I claims a single sequence of affine maps {A_i, A^{out}_i} in Aff_{<=5d} such that every update h_k factors through the shared prefix (ReLU o A_{k-1}) o ... o (ReLU o A_1) — the property that makes the construction an MGDL network rather than an arbitrary sum of bumps. This simultaneous factorization is nontrivial: each block must pass the original input through the ReLU bottleneck (possible only because x >= 0 on [0,1]^d, a fact never mentioned) while computing its own bump's 4d ridge terms, and in the proof of Theorem 1.1 later stages' blocks must additionally compose through all previously frozen blocks. No formulas, induction, or channel accounting are given; the only justification is an external figure and a schematic remark about 'fake layers'. The width bound 5d is therefore unverified, and the cross-stage stacking in 'Proceeding recursively, the same argument can be applied' is never addressed.

issues.failure_explanation: The strategy section claims the construction achieves the pointwise bound |g(x) - Sg(x)| <= (1-eps)|g(x)| for every x. The formal argument (Lemma 4.2, and its use in Theorem 3.1) establishes only the uniform-norm bound ||g - Sg||_infinity <= (1-eps)||g||_infinity. The pointwise version is false for the constructed operator: near the edge of a dilated cube rQ the cutoff Gamma_Q(x) is arbitrarily close to 0 while the choice of delta guarantees only g(x) >= 2^d eps ||g||_infinity > 0 there, so |g(x) - Sg(x)| = g(x) - eps||g||_infinity Gamma_Q(x) is arbitrarily close to g(x), which exceeds (1-eps)g(x) on a set of positive measure (e.g., a one-dimensional target ramping down from its peak at the maximal rate allowed by the modulus of continuity). What actually holds pointwise is only domination |g - Sg| <= |g|.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition requires Gamma_Q(x) = 0 for x outside rQ, but with Gamma_Q(x) = (1/d) sum_j psi(2(x_j - c_j)/ell(Q)) the value is zero only where every coordinate satisfies |y_j| >= r. For d >= 2, a point with one coordinate inside the slab still gets a positive value: e.g., d = 2, x_1 = c_1(Q) (so psi(y_1) = 1) and |x_2 - c_2(Q)| > r ell(Q)/2 gives Gamma_Q(x) = 1/2 although x is not in rQ. Hence each 'cutoff' is supported on a union of slabs, not on rQ: the number of cutoffs active at a point is not bounded by 2^d but grows with the number of cubes (order delta^{-(d-1)} per slab direction, unbounded as delta -> 0), so the estimate sum_i Gamma_i(x) <= 2^d and the claim 'Gamma_{Q_i}(x) = 0 for x notin union rQ_i' in Lemma 4.5 are false, condition (C1) (0 <= T_eps g <= g^+) fails, and the sign separation 'h_k(x) = 0 for x in Omega_2' used for pointwise domination fails. Lemma 4.5's conclusion is false for the constructed operator (T_eps g can exceed g^+ by an arbitrarily large factor), and the defect propagates to Theorem 3.1, Theorem 1.1, and Corollary 1.2. The localization also cannot be repaired within one-hidden-layer grade blocks: in d >= 2 no nonzero compactly supported function is representable as A^{out} o ReLU o A (each hidden unit kinks along an entire hyperplane, which would meet the region where the function must vanish); the standard correction tilde-Psi(x) = max{0, sum_j psi(x_j) - (d-1)} requires a second ReLU layer per grade. For d = 1 the average coincides with psi and is a valid cutoff; the defect is specific to d >= 2.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Psi by tilde-Psi(x) = max{0, sum_{j=1}^d psi(x_j) - (d-1)}, which equals 1 exactly on Q, takes values in [0,1], and is supported in rQ; realize it by carrying the input through the blocks and applying the outer ReLU one layer after the four per-coordinate terms, restating the architecture accordingly (e.g., width 5d+1 with the same prefix-sum MGDL formula and strict decay from grade 2, or width 5d with two affine-ReLU units per grade and monotonicity asserted per grade). The overlap lemma, the contraction and symmetrization arguments, and the iteration then go through unchanged, preserving the (1-eps) contraction factor, fixed width, and strictly decaying residuals per grade.
issues.overall_effect: The whole contraction argument in dimension d >= 2 (Lemma 4.5, hence Theorem 3.1, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2) is invalidated: the uniform overlap bound, the pointwise domination 0 <= T_eps g <= g^+, and the per-grade sign separation all rest on the false support property of Gamma_Q.
issues.title: Averaged Psi does not produce a cube cutoff: Gamma_Q does not vanish outside rQ in d >= 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained new construction plus a limited restatement of the architecture (an extra ReLU layer per grade and width/index bookkeeping), leaving a recognizably comparable theorem — same MGDL framework, fixed width, contraction factor, and monotone vanishing residuals — without new global proof architecture; however it is more than a routine fix, because the stated one-hidden-layer-per-grade version provably cannot produce localized cutoffs in d >= 2 and must be modified.
